findings.title: Team admin check uses && with isTeamOwner, so only users who are both admin and owner pass
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. A team admin who is not the owner, or an owner who is not an admin, fails this check. The name says "admin or owner", so this should be `||`. As written, team admins who are not owners get FORBIDDEN unless they are also attendees or the organizer.

findings.title: Blacklist check is case-sensitive while the blacklist is lowercased
findings.body: The blacklist is built with `.toLowerCase()`, but the guest is compared as-is with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. An input such as `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses a blacklist entry `blocked@example.com`. The attendee duplicate check on line 76 is also case-sensitive, so the same address in a different case can be added as a second attendee.

findings.title: Duplicate guests within the same request are not removed server-side
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` only filters against existing attendees and the blacklist. If `guests` contains the same address twice (the schema in addGuests.schema.ts does not enforce uniqueness, and the client-side check can be bypassed), both rows go into `createMany` and the booking gets duplicate attendee rows, which then produce duplicate invites and emails.

findings.title: Calendar update failure after DB write leaves guests added but reports an error
findings.body: The attendees are persisted at line 92 before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs at line 165, which is not wrapped in try/catch. If the calendar update throws, the client gets an error and the dialog stays open, yet the guests are already saved in the database. A retry then hits the 'no unique guests' path. The DB write and calendar sync are not atomic, and the failure mode is not handled.

findings.title: Email failure is swallowed with a bare console.log and no error detail
findings.body: The catch block logs only the fixed string "Error sending AddGuestsEmails" and discards `err`, so the cause of email failures is lost. Other code in the repo uses the logger for this. Consider logging the error through the shared logger.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores eventType disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: Every other send function in this file checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` (or the hostEmailDisabled flags) before sending. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no event type metadata and always emails the organizer, team members, and all attendees. Hosts who disabled standard emails will still receive these notifications.

findings.title: Subject uses attendees[0] name, which is empty for newly added guests
findings.body: New guests are created with `name: ""`, and the organizer email subject in organizer-add-guests-email.ts uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. If the first attendee is a newly added guest, or the existing first attendee has no name, the subject is rendered with a blank name. The subject-building logic should fall back to a sensible value, such as the organizer name or the attendee email.

findings.title: Invalid-email error is never cleared after a later valid submit
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on a failed validation, but it is reset only by the Cancel button. After the user fixes the emails and clicks Add, the mutation runs and the stale error message stays visible, including after a successful add (onSuccess at line 36 does not reset it).

findings.title: Hardcoded English tooltip text bypasses i18n
findings.body: The remove-button tooltip is the literal string "Remove email", while the surrounding labels all go through `t()`. Non-English users will see English text here.

findings.title: Error message concatenates the tRPC error code into the toast
findings.body: The toast message is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, so users see text like "FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission". Also `t()` is called on raw server message keys such as `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which may not exist in every locale. The fallback `t("unable_to_add_guests")` is effectively unreachable because the template string is always truthy.
